text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. To achieve this, developers should follow clear naming conventions, such as using meaningful variable names like "totalPrice" instead of "x". Functions should also be small and do only one job, which makes them easier to test and reuse. In addition, clean code is much easier to maintain, because other developers can quickly find and fix problems. Although writing clean code takes more time at the beginning, it saves a lot of effort in the long run.
